requirement_text.REQ-124: MOB-2 (docs/mobile/requirements.md) needs GET /tenant-config to return { realm_url, locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind } WITHOUT a bearer token: the mobile app calls it to discover which realm to authenticate against, so by definition it has no token yet. Verified against lib/ on 2026-08-21, this is two gaps, not one: (a) Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig is a stub whose routes land in REQ-078; and (b) Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline mounts it behind Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, so implementing the route is not sufficient -- it would still demand the token the caller cannot have. Resolve (b) explicitly: either an unauthenticated variant mounted ahead of AuthPipeline, or a documented exemption inside it. Pick one and record why in the moduledoc. This is the gate for the entire mobile tier -- without it the app cannot reach a login screen -- which is why it is sequenced first in docs/mobile/build-order.md phase M-0. Security scope: an unauthenticated endpoint returning per-tenant data is a tenant-data path by definition and needs SECURITY-REVIEWER. The response must expose only what bootstrap requires. Check the shape field-by-field against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md -- in particular whether an unauthenticated caller enumerating slugs can learn which tenants exist, and what the answer should be for a slug that does not exist.

task.description: Run scripts/test_parallel.sh -- the full suite, not just the new tests -- per WF-02 Step 4's standard procedure. If no local toolchain, use the Docker fallback documented in docs/anti-patterns.md; report explicitly if neither is available rather than reporting PASS without having run it. Write test/reports/report-<date>-WF02-REQ124-20260822.yaml with the actual output, including the derived partition count N, its source, and the combined pass/fail totals. Any failure caused by this run's own implementation is reworked on this branch (route back to ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER as appropriate). Any failure NOT attributable to this branch must be attributed structurally per core-directives.md's 'Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching' -- name the evidence (diff doesn't touch the failing module/deps, OR reproduced at merge-base with output quoted, OR a demonstrated external mechanism with a measurement) -- never by matching a previously-reported count or set. A failure with no existing issue record is reported for filing, not silently folded into 'the known set' -- you report the finding, ORCH files it.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/test_parallel.sh run to completion with real, quoted output
Combined pass/fail totals reported, with partition count N and its source
Every failure attributed to either this branch (rework) or pre-existing (structural evidence named, one of the three forms) -- no unattributed failure silently ignored
